scope: Research other games' frame-rate optimization methods, review the pending map/particle changes, and decide whether further work should delay merging main.
decision: Finish the narrowly scoped empty-particle-emitter fast path and merge the current map/particle optimizations. Further frame-rate work needs target-device profiling; this is not a claim that no future optimization is possible.

sources.title: Riot: Performance Boost — VALORANT's Global Invalidation
sources.lesson: Cache unchanged UI and update only invalidated elements; validate gains across representative hardware.
sources.application: Covered hall DOM hiding, shared HUD RAF, and value-based UI updates already address this class of work; no further actionable HUD defect was identified.

sources.title: PlayCanvas: General Guidelines
sources.lesson: Reuse temporary objects, control draw-call overhead, and balance visibility-test cost against the work it saves.
sources.application: Keep batch count stable during map instance compaction. Preserve pooling and active-prefix particle uploads. Add only the verified empty-emitter allocation fast path.

sources.title: Epic: Niagara Scalability and Best Practices
sources.lesson: Effect instances and emitters have overhead; pooling and system reuse reduce allocation, but finer culling and CPU/GPU simulation choices have tradeoffs.
sources.application: Retain pooled effects and skip empty passes. Do not enable extra batching or move small particle simulations to the GPU without project-specific evidence.

sources.title: Unity: Performance profiling tips for game developers
sources.lesson: Establish a baseline, work to a frame-time budget, and measure CPU/GPU stages before and after changes.
sources.application: Use isolated fixed-input comparisons and frame-time distributions. Triangle counts, mock GL byte counts, and CPU submission time do not establish presented-frame or hardware FPS gains.

sources.title: Fortnite: Performance Mode Boosts PC FPS
sources.lesson: An optional lower-quality mode can reduce memory and CPU/GPU work.
sources.application: Do not silently reduce this project's texture sizes, particle appearance, resolution, shadows or animation. Treat a future quality preset as a separate product choice.

sources.title: MDN: WebGL best practices
sources.lesson: Synchronous WebGL queries can stall; reduce avoidable work and use diagnostics carefully.
sources.application: Production excludes diagnostic probes. GPU timing and GL call instrumentation remain explicit opt-ins; do not add synchronization to chase an unconfirmed long-frame cause.

additionalChange.action: Return zero before allocating scratch vectors and a scratch matrix; preserve the outer render function's cleanup and state restoration.
additionalChange.evidence: Read-only audit observed 240 scratch Float32Array constructions for 240 empty calls and identified 13 additional vector-array initializers per call. Tests exercise the retained native emitter and nonempty GPU vertex output.

deferred: LOD, different spatial batches, transparency/composite scissoring and texture compression require target-GPU measurements and visual validation.
Worker/WebGPU rendering or GPU particle simulation would be architectural work without a demonstrated bottleneck.
Prior full spatial splitting increased draw calls and regressed measured frame rate; leave it disabled.

validation.review: Independent review found no blocking regression in map compaction, shadow restoration, replay isolation or diagnostic separation.
validation.note: Final automated test and offline verification results are recorded in README.md and verification.json.
